title: Make a goal reachable from a lower start
objectives: Show how a step-up lowers the starting SIP needed for a goal.
Explain who benefits most from that trade-off.
body_md:
The most practical use of a step-up is making a goal reachable today.

## Goal: ₹1 crore in 15 years (illustrative, 12% a year assumed)

| Approach | Starting monthly SIP needed |
|---|---|
| Flat SIP | ≈ ₹19,800 |
| SIP with a 10% yearly step-up | ≈ ₹11,500 |

A step-up lets a young client start with what they can afford today, and let rising income do the rest.

## Who benefits most

- Clients early in their careers, whose income will grow faster than their expenses.
- Clients who cannot start at ₹19,800 today but can start at ₹11,500 and grow into it.
- Clients who dislike big commitments: the start is smaller and the cap makes it bounded.

## What to tell them

The ₹11,500 is not a magic number; it is an illustration at 12% a year. Show the assumption and the total invested, and make no promise that the goal will be reached.
example: Karan wants ₹1 crore in 15 years but can afford ₹12,000 a month. A 10% yearly step-up starting around ₹11,500 fits today's cash flow, at an assumed 12%, with no guarantee.
say: A step-up lets you start at about ₹11,500 instead of ₹19,800 for the same illustrative goal.
The figure assumes 12% a year; it is an illustration, not a promise.
never: The step-up removes the need to review the goal.
